items.abstract_or_text: 最近看到佐治亚理工 2026 年的 LLM 课程，光看课表就很值得收藏。 它很像一份已经帮你筛过一遍的「2026 大模型前沿论文阅读清单」。 前面还有 Pretraining、Embedding、MoE 这些基础，但很快就进入 Agent Harness、GRPO、DAPO、自博弈 RL、Test-Time Scaling、Long Context。 后面甚至已经排到了 Linear Transformer、Diffusion LM、模型安全和 Mechanistic Interpretability。 DeepSeek-V2、DeepSeek-V3.2、OpenHands、Absolute Zero 这些最近经常讨论的工作，也直接进了课程。 我觉得这份课表很能说明现在 LLM 研究在关注什么。 训练一个更大的模型依然重要，但推理怎么扩展、Agent 怎么使用工具和记忆、模型怎么靠 RL 和环境交互继续提升，已经占了相当大的篇幅。 如果最近经常看到 GRPO、Self-Play、Agent Harness 这些词，却一直没找到一条比较完整的学习路线，可以直接顺着这份课表一篇篇读。 课程资源

items.title: @marfinxx：This Stanford and MIT paper is f*cking insane A new research paper proves that optimizing the Python harness around an L
items.abstract_or_text: This Stanford and MIT paper is f*cking insane A new research paper proves that optimizing the Python harness around an LLM produces up to a 6x performance gap without changing model weights The result: outer-loop coding agent search, unrestricted filesystem access to 10M trace tokens, and self-evolving context architectures execution trace logs → filesystem grep diagnosis → causal failure isolation → outer-loop code rewrite → Pareto-optimized harness Stanford researchers introduced Meta-Harness, an automated system that evolves the code governing context, memory, and retrieval: → Full Diagnostic Trace Access Replaces lossy scalar scores and short summaries with full filesystem access. An agentic proposer inspects raw execution logs and source code across past iterations using grep and cat → Causal Failure Analysis in Code Space Instead of tweaking prompt words, the system isolates confounded regressions, traces downstream errors to early context decisions, and rewrites executable Python functions → 4x Token Compression with Higher Accuracy Discovered context management policies beat state-of-the-art agentic memory systems by 7.7 points while using 4x fewer context tokens, converging 10x faster than traditional optimizers → Zero-Shot Transfer Across Unseen Models A single discovered math retrieval harness improved solve rates on 200 IMO-level olympiad problems by 4.7 points across five completely held-out frontier models → Hypothesis Verification & Empirical Results Stanford hypothesized that code-space optimization with raw execution trace access beats compressed prompt tuning. Practical validation on production agent pipelines confirmed the findings: classification accuracy improved by 7.7 points while context token overhead plummeted by 75% The code surrounding the model matters as much as the weights themselves. Automating harness engineering bridges frozen LLMs with self-improving cognitive systems

items.title: @dair_ai：Great paper if you are building production-grade agents. It's a good way to understand what is actually incurring costs
items.abstract_or_text: Great paper if you are building production-grade agents. It's a good way to understand what is actually incurring costs in your agents, which involve more complex components and decisions. This works finds that across ten instrumented agentic applications, non-LLM components dominate latency in five of them. Sandbox working sets peak at 28 GB per session. Task latencies inside one application diverge by up to 32x across GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, and CPU-bound sandboxes. Production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps. Auxiliary LLM calls and tool schema overhead form a control-plane tax that crowds out productive compute. Task-aware serving cuts latency 29 to 40%, state offloading cuts memory 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls. Paper: https://t.co/USjtnI9DvE

items.title: @DrJimFan：Seeing a hype wave around GEN-1.5, and rightfully so. Lots of respect to Pete & Andy for executing so well. The secret i
items.abstract_or_text: Seeing a hype wave around GEN-1.5, and rightfully so. Lots of respect to Pete & Andy for executing so well. The secret is in the naturally repetitive motions in human-collected data. There're 2 main sources for such repetitions: (1) Symmetric patterns. Sorting, tidying, and assembling almost never finish in one motion. Open any assembly manual from IKEA, and you find most objects symmetrical. You drive one bolt, then its twin, then the next pair. Every {bolt A, bolt B} pair is a natural continuation in context, and the second instance is a free training signal that imitates the first ("prompt"). (2) Recovery. Humans drop things all the time, but we pick them up so fast, we don’t even notice. That reflex to fix is half of our physical competence. The key insight is to keep the failed first half instead of trimming it away. If the model consumes the full arc, fumble, catch, continue, then recovery shows up organically at test time. It's funny that in-context improvement results from *NOT* over-sanitizing your data. The other critical ingredient is UMI. I've been saying for a while that teleop will not last, and GEN-1.5 is driving the final nail in the coffin. UMI is essentially a human wearing the robot gripper to collect data directly (human → data). Teleop inserts a layer of separation: human → VR/skeletal device → robot → data, which bleeds out all the human "physical intuition". The subtle sleight of hand we perform constantly with objects, the micro-adjustments, the feel of a part snapping into place, is nearly impossible to capture when you can't feel the environment directly. Once you have enough data, many behaviors can actually be zero-shot. For example, you don't even need finetuning to pick up a novel object. The model "just knows" what to do given a similar scene in the training distribution. Whether in-context learning truly works or not also depends on how far away the test is from training. Currently, the demos are still a bit too simple to conclude. I'm cautiously optimistic. Still, it's a great day in robotics.

items.title: @GeneralistAI：Experiments across 10 diverse tasks show 59% average success with one-shot physical prompting, straight from pretraining
items.abstract_or_text: Experiments across 10 diverse tasks show 59% average success with one-shot physical prompting, straight from pretraining. With few-shot learning, performance rises to 83% via 10 gradient steps on 5 minutes of data per task. Although the tasks are simple and success rates are modest, it’s the first model we know of that exhibits the general ability to learn a wide range of dexterous closed-loop physical tasks from just one or few demonstrations. This accelerates reaching a base level of competence for new skills that can be subsequently refined towards mastery.

items.abstract_or_text: 我想，机器人领域可能刚刚迎来了自己的GPT-3时刻。 Generalist AI刚刚发布了新一代机器人基础模型GEN-1.5，第一次把大模型里的One-shot In-context Learning大规模搬进了物理世界： 你给机器人现场演示一遍，它几秒钟就能学会，不训练，也不微调。 GEN-1.5拥有30秒的上下文记忆，只需要看一次3～12秒的动作演示，就能立刻执行新的物理任务。10个不同任务里，One-shot平均成功率已经达到59%。 如果愿意稍微训练一下，成本也低得离谱：只需要5分钟数据、约50次演示、10个gradient steps，平均成功率就能提高到83%。 Generalist把这个东西叫做：Physical Prompting，物理Prompt。

items.title: @AnthropicAI：Many drugs work by binding to a specific target in the body and blocking or changing what it does. An important first st
items.abstract_or_text: Many drugs work by binding to a specific target in the body and blocking or changing what it does. An important first step in the drug development process is designing a molecule that can bind tightly to its target. Traditionally, that's meant weeks or months of expert work per target, sifting through a large number of candidates to identify the few that work. We wanted to test if Claude could successfully design novel protein binders from scratch (also called de novo design). With a protein design prompt written by a human expert, Claude autonomously designed protein binders against 14 out of 15 targets. We then worked with Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience, who independently built and tested the proteins Claude designed.

items.title: @AnthropicAI：Designing a binder is an easier process than designing a drug, but it’s a useful proxy. The typical success rate in the
items.abstract_or_text: Designing a binder is an easier process than designing a drug, but it’s a useful proxy. The typical success rate in the field today is between 10% and 15%. Between 22% and 35% of Claude's designs bound successfully, depending on the setup. Some of its strongest designs bound several times more tightly than the best published de novo binder.

items.title: @AnthropicAI：Importantly, protein binders are not drugs. Designing a high-affinity binder is just the first step in the process of de
items.abstract_or_text: Importantly, protein binders are not drugs. Designing a high-affinity binder is just the first step in the process of developing a drug-like molecule. Even designing a drug itself is just one phase out of the many required to establish that a drug is safe and effective before making it available to people. However, this establishes a strong foundation to work from, and we are building on it by teaching Claude to run the entire development process end-to-end for every major type of drug molecule—from antibodies to small molecules.

items.abstract_or_text: 分享一个比较有意思的研究。 研究者训练了一个「只学到小学五年级」的语言模型 LittleLearner。 他们先做了一个 88B Token 的训练集，把五年级以上的概念、知识和词汇尽量过滤掉，再从头训练一个 5B 模型。 效果挺有意思。 问它什么是重力，它可以正常回答。 问「薛定谔的猫」，它会告诉你，这是一只「长着两张脸的猫」。 但这个项目真正有价值的地方，是可以比较干净地研究一个问题。 模型经过 SFT、RL、Few-shot 之后能力变强，到底是真的学到了新能力，还是把预训练里已经存在的东西重新激活了。 他们把模型从 0.6B 扩到 5B，又试了 SFT + GRPO 和 ICL。 结果基本一致。 训练范围内的能力会继续提升，但一旦进入真正没学过的高年级知识，单纯扩大模型、做 RL 或给几个示例，都很难跨过原来的边界。 论文 https://t.co/lW28SDGpIc 项目

items.title: @ericxing：As made clearly in my post, what qualifies as a minimum virtual cell must meet 4 minimum features: 1) multi-modal, meani
items.abstract_or_text: As made clearly in my post, what qualifies as a minimum virtual cell must meet 4 minimum features: 1) multi-modal, meaning simulating across all data types including sequence, structure, transcriptome, localization, morphology, etc, all at the same time for the same cell state; 2) multi-scale, from DNA, RNA, Protein, all the way to full cell snd beyond (such as tissue in later releases) all at once; 3) dynamic — can continuously roll forward, backward, branch, upon consecutive interventions of different kinds; 4) stateful — remembers its cellular conditions, allowing reversible or counterfactual manipulations. In summary, a VC is holistic simulator, not a one shot predictor, therefore we create it with world model, not any single LLM-based next token prediction foundation models. Hope this helps. You are welcome to read our accompanying technical report or our recent AIDO paper on @NatureMedicine for more details.

items.title: @marinkazitnik：Do LLMs know when they have enough information to answer, and what to ask a human when they don’t? @_yepeng We spend a l
items.abstract_or_text: Do LLMs know when they have enough information to answer, and what to ask a human when they don’t? @_yepeng We spend a lot of time developing agents that can answer the questions we ask them. But the reverse direction gets much less attention: when the prompt does not contain enough information, can a model recognize what is missing and ask for it? Paper: https://t.co/xlWmIwZ4Mt Project: https://t.co/tY06kTBsyp For agents that interact with humans, biological systems, or clinical workflows, we need to evaluate not only whether they can answer questions, but also whether they know what they need to know before answering. (1) Consider an agent evaluating a patient with pelvic pain. The duration of the pain determines which diagnostic pathway applies, so until the agent asks about it, no downstream symptom or test is clearly relevant. (2) Now consider an agent reasoning about a gene regulatory network, where the outcome depends on the unknown states of several genes. Acquiring one of them can leave several outcomes possible, so the agent must identify the full set that determines the outcome. Both cases raise the same three questions. Does the model recognize that information is missing? Does it identify which information it needs? Does it know when it has enough to answer?

items.title: @BiologyAIDaily：AlphaConformers: Structure-guided sampling enables prediction of multiple protein conformations 1. The paper presents Al
items.abstract_or_text: AlphaConformers: Structure-guided sampling enables prediction of multiple protein conformations 1. The paper presents AlphaConformers, a structure-guided pipeline that steers AlphaFold2 (AF2) toward alternative protein conformations (apo/holo), addressing AF2’s tendency to collapse to a single preferred state (often holo-like). 2. Core idea: structural databases (PDB + AlphaFold DB) implicitly capture the conformational space accessible to a protein family; by harvesting that diversity from structurally similar proteins, one can generate “conformational hypotheses” for a target and feed them to AF2. Main performance takeaway: AlphaConformers’ strongest advantage is for subtle apo-holo rearrangements (<2 Å). Against an AF2 baseline (25 models with dropout), AlphaConformers improves recovery substantially on the subtle set (apo: 53.8% vs 23.1%; holo: 46.2% vs 19.2%). 💻Code: https://t.co/F6He6nBqMl 📜Paper: https://t.co/9mggRWuUo4

items.abstract_or_text: Protein structure prediction: From evolutionary constraints to generative modeling This review reframes the “AlphaFold era” as a methodological evolution rather than a leaderboard story, organizing progress into four phases plus three cross-cutting transitions that explain why today’s models can do more than monomer folding. Phase II (end-to-end deep folding) is exemplified by AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold. Phase III expands to complexes, protein–nucleic acid systems, and all-atom heterogeneous systems including ligands (RoseTTAFold All-Atom, AlphaFold3). Phase IV covers generative modeling for design (RFdiffusion, La-Proteina). 📜Paper: https://t.co/zpxv7SS4dC
